aspect: It attaches to specific acts, which is what makes it durable
description: General guilt fades. 'I took the last seat in the car' does not, because it is true, and no amount of reframing makes it untrue.
energy_note: A fact about yourself you cannot argue with.

aspect: Guilt for the freedoms you now have
description: Named directly in diaspora clinical writing: guilt for the safety you enjoy, intensified by the belief that you are not doing enough, until the privilege of being safe becomes too heavy to carry.
energy_note: Safety as a thing you owe money on.

description: Sabotaging a promotion, ending a good relationship, refusing treatment. The mechanism is a felt conviction that comfort is not permitted, and it is almost never articulated as that.
money_note: Career and relationship costs of unrecognised self-sabotage.
energy_note: Quietly declining a life you think you have not earned.

aspect: It cannot be relieved by the people it concerns
description: The dead cannot absolve. The survivors in the country say 'don't be silly', which does not land. There is no one with standing to grant the pardon.
energy_note: A debt with no creditor to pay.

description: Justifying the survival through achievement. Effective for a decade, then it collapses, usually as burnout, usually diagnosed as depression with no reference to the war at all.
energy_note: Twelve productive years and a wall at the end of them.
